title: Orchestrate Private data-plane runtime upgrades with zero-downtime rollouts and deterministic rollback
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers running Redwood Private in customer VPCs require automated runtime/data-plane upgrades that guarantee zero-downtime for in-flight requests, preserve KV/prefix cache correctness, and allow deterministic, fast rollback when regressions are detected. Current upgrade flows are manual, error-prone, and risk customer traffic disruption and stale cache issues.

Goal: Build an orchestrated, IaC-driven upgrade flow for the data plane/runtime that: (1) runs via Terraform/Terraform modules and CI pipelines, (2) performs incremental canary rollouts with traffic steering and health evaluation, (3) supports transactional rollback to a known-good runtime image without loss of availability, and (4) integrates runtime health checks, KV cache warmup, and observability hooks for automatic decisioning.

Scope: This ticket focuses on the data-plane/runtime layer in Private deployments (not control plane) and covers orchestration, health probes, cache warming, routable traffic policies, and rollback automation. Work spans Terraform module hooks, operator/controller changes in the on-prem runtime manager, and CI pipeline integration.

Out of scope: model checkpoints, customer-specific app upgrades, and storage migrations beyond ephemeral runtime state.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform-driven upgrade pipeline can trigger a canary rollout of runtime image X.Y to a single node pool in a VPC environment
Canary receives <= 5% traffic and automatically escalates to 25%/50%/100% based on health gates within configured time windows
Health gates include: request success rate >= 99.5% over a 2m window, 95th latency < configured SLO, KV cache hit-rate >= baseline after warmup, and no increase in error-class 'model-mismatch'
Rollback automated decision can revert 100% of traffic to previous image within 30s with no dropped or misrouted in-flight responses
Terraform module exposes flags: canary_percentage, gate_conditions, snapshot_before_upgrade, and forced_rollback_timeout
Integration tests (local and e2e in staging) exercise failure modes and show no 5xx spikes during graceful drain
Documentation and runbook updated with step-by-step rollback and troubleshooting checklist
tasks: Design canary traffic steering and deterministic routing strategy (operator + LB rules)
Add Terraform module hooks to create rollout resources and record image history snapshots
Implement drain protocol in runtime agent: stop new requests, complete in-flight, flush/serialize cache checkpoint if configured
Build cache-warm path: pre-warm KV/prefix with representative prompts and validate hit-rate metric
Create health gate evaluator service that consumes telemetry and triggers rollout progression/rollback
Implement fast rollback path that atomically switches routes to previous deployment and re-hydrates cache snapshot
Add CI pipeline job to run staged rollout in staging and collect baseline metrics
End-to-end tests: canary pass, canary fail -> rollback, and rollback re-verify
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: KV-cache warming might be slow and cause higher latency for early users. Mitigation: allow snapshot restore from previous image and parallel async warm using background workers; measure warming time and gate promotion until hit-rate met.

Risk: Traffic steering mismatch across network LB and runtime leads to split-brain. Mitigation: use single source-of-truth controller to update both LB and runtime routing; add reconciliation loop and pre-checks in Terraform plan/apply.
Risk: Terraform state drift between customer VPC and operator expectations. Mitigation: multi-step apply with validation phase and read-only dry-run mode exposed to customers before live upgrades.

Risk: Rollback causing cache incompatibility across runtime versions. Mitigation: require runtime image semantic version compatibility, and if incompatible, perform blue-green-style full node replacement with cache snapshot/restore where possible.
